solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Junior sports team member lapping graduate, a blue

indicators.note: lapping means going round, so the team member wraps itself around the graduate

parts.note: a colt is a young player in a junior team
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A young player overtakes a graduate athlete who has won a university blue.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'a blue' is an Oxbridge sporting honour; here it is a shade. A colt is a junior player, a usage from British school sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a deep shade of the colour, so it is one example of a blue.

clue.text: Conservative seeking victory

parts.note: a quest is a seeking or search

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is hungry for an election win.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a winning of something by force or effort, a synonym for triumph.

clue.text: Gambler on cricket side becomes richer

parts.note: a better is one who bets
off is one side of the cricket field, opposite leg

explanation.surface: A punter backing a cricket team wins and grows wealthier.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being better off is an idiom for having more money, so it means wealthier.

clue.text: Cavalryman about, in country road on right

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for about sits inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow country road
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A horse soldier rides about on the right of a country road.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer was a mounted soldier armed with a lance, a type of cavalry trooper.

clue.text: Dramatist in bar having usual drink at first

parts.note: to bar is to stop
par is the normal or usual level

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word drink is used

explanation.surface: A playwright sits in a pub with their usual tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bar' tempts as a container; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Stoppard is a celebrated British playwright, so he is an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: Three crossing quiet river (small) listen for fish

indicators.note: crossing means the word three lies across, so around, the quiet signal

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
hark means listen

explanation.surface: Three people wade a quiet little river, listening out for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The thresher shark is a long-tailed shark, and a shark is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Objection made by expert on trial

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: An expert witness raises an objection in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' suggests a courtroom; it is just a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is an expression of disapproval, so it is a synonym for objection.

clue.text: Plus point when fixed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
set means fixed or established

explanation.surface: Something becomes an advantage once it is repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or advantage, so it is a plus point.

clue.text: Poet in study, in need of a drink first

indicators.note: first puts the word for thirsty before the study

parts.note: dry means thirsty, in need of a drink
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A poet working in his study wants a drink before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the English poet laureate of the 17th century, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Unacceptable concept I rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the letter I is thrown out of the word for the concept

parts.note: a concept is a notion

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an idea as beyond the pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is 'not on' is an informal idiom meaning it is not allowed or acceptable.

clue.text: Spoonerism in essence, produced by broadcaster

parts.note: the marrow of something is its core or essence
Sky is a British television broadcaster

explanation.surface: A broadcaster airs a slip of the tongue that gets to the heart of things.
explanation.walkthrough: SKY is a British satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: A marrowsky is an old slang word for a transposition of initial sounds, the same slip named after Rev Spooner.

clue.text: Annie, perhaps, presides over game

parts.note: Annie is a stage musical, hence perhaps
to chair a meeting is to preside over it

explanation.surface: A girl called Annie seems to be running the party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annie' looks like a person; it is the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical chairs is a party game where players scramble for seats when the music stops.

clue.text: Ineffectual advice from a conservationist?

definitions.meaning: having no effect, of no practical help
read as two words, the instruction to consume fewer resources

explanation.surface: Mocks a conservationist whose advice achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without effect is of no practical value, and split in two the word is a plea to consume less.

clue.text: Form of respect for ghost

indicators.note: a form of a word is a version of it reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows deference toward a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is an apparition or spirit, a direct synonym for a phantom.

clue.text: Appear in a theatrical production

definitions.meaning: to turn up or become visible

explanation.surface: An actor is cast in a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is to make an appearance, and a staged performance is a familiar sense too.

clue.text: Bottle party during stay

indicators.note: during means the party is placed in the middle of the word for stay

parts.note: to stay is to stop
a crew is a group or party of people

explanation.surface: A bottle is opened at a party while staying somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwtop is a bottle closed with a threaded cap, so the word names that kind of container.

clue.text: Maiden is taken in by pitiful fortune-telling

indicators.note: taken in by means maiden and is are held inside the word for pitiful

parts.note: paltry means pitiful or meagre
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman is duped by a shabby fortune-teller.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry is reading the lines of the hand to foretell the future, one form of fortune-telling.

clue.text: Look over church on headland, Scottish landmark

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the word for look above the church

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A sightseer surveys a church on a headland in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous loch near Inverness, home of the legendary monster, is a well-known feature of Scotland.

clue.text: Perfect female canon, shorter

parts.note: a canon is a rule or law
less in length means shorter

explanation.surface: Praises a woman cleric whose sermon was mercifully brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' reads as a clergyman; here it is a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without any defect or blemish is perfect, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: A series under discussion

parts.note: a tissue is a connected series, as in a tissue of lies

explanation.surface: A set of programmes is being debated.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point currently being debated or disputed.

clue.text: Further, therefore, by a length

parts.note: so means therefore

explanation.surface: A list of reasoning words with a length thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce an extra point, meaning in addition or furthermore.

clue.text: Shy type consuming second light dessert

indicators.note: consuming means the shy type swallows the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a mouse is a timid, shy person

explanation.surface: A timid person helps themselves to a second pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a frothy, airy sweet dish, so it is a light pudding.

clue.text: Maelstrom: series of letters from survivor, Texan

indicators.note: series of letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Texan survives a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, and a vortex is a whirling mass of water or air.

clue.text: Flightless bird — I check on unfamiliar sort

indicators.note: unfamiliar means the word sort appears in a strange new arrangement

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone inspects an odd-looking bird that cannot fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest bird and cannot fly, so it fits the description exactly.

clue.text: Vagrant in vehicle close to tip

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word tip is used

explanation.surface: A homeless man rides a vehicle near the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is a British word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer, so a vagrant.

clue.text: Do away with blood group O? Is hospital to follow line?

parts.note: AB is one of the blood groups

explanation.surface: A medical query about blood type and hospital procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' just means IS H comes after L.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to put an end to something formally, a synonym for doing away with it.

clue.text: Criticism involving drinks farce

indicators.note: involving means the drinks are wrapped inside the word for criticism

parts.note: to get stick is to receive criticism
an animal laps when it drinks

explanation.surface: A boozy evening ends in an embarrassing comic fiasco that draws criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy, the stock stuff of a stage farce.

clue.text: Let it out, showing evidence of ownership

indicators.note: out signals the words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to reveal their proof of who owns a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal title is the document or right establishing that a property belongs to someone.

clue.text: Entrepreneur, primarily for that reason, bringing journalists in for coffee

indicators.note: primarily means only the leading letter of the word entrepreneur is taken
in means the journalists are put inside the word for that reason

parts.note: so means for that reason
the press are journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A businessman invites reporters round for a cup of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Looks after neat flowers

indicators.note: after places the word for looks behind the word for neat

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
to eye is to look at, so eyes means looks

explanation.surface: Someone takes care of tidy flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' reads as tidy; it is the old word for a bovine.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye is a daisy-like plant, so the plural names those blooms.
